To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cumulative-deuteron spectra in 16Op reactions at 3.25 AGeV are described by the parameter T0=0.25±0.05 GeV/c2 and that the contribution of the decay of alpha-particle clusters to the production of cumulative deuterrons in this reaction is about 20% of the total production.

cumulative deuterons can be formed as a result of slow-pion absorption in alpha-particle clusters of nuclei and that the contribution to cumulative-deuterons production from this source is comparable with the contribution from other sources.

we have measured for the first time the production of cumulative deuterium nuclei in 16Op reactions at a momentum of P = 3.25 A GeV/c and that we have determined the parameter T0 characterising the slope of the spectra of invariant cross sections.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the production of cumulative nuclei in collisions of oxygen ions with protons at 3.25 and 6.5 GeV/c per ion.
the study of the production of cumulative deuterium nuclei in 16Op reactions at a momentum of p = 3.25GeV/c per nucleon under the condition of a 4 π acceptance.
the study of cumulative nuclei production in 16Op interactions at a momentum of p= 3.25GeV/c per nucleon in a 4π geometry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the production of cumulative deuterium in the interaction of oxygen nuclei with the proton at a momentum of p = 3.25 ± 0.1 GeV/c per particle is determined by the decay of clusters in the nuclei upon slow-particle absorption.
the cumulative production is due to the absorption of slow pions by the target nuclei.

the cumulative production of deuterons in 16Op reactions at a momentum of ~3.25 Gev/c per nucleon can be satisfactorily explained in the framework of the model of slow-pion absorption on alpha-particle clusters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the processes of the decay of clusters in nuclei upon pion absorption are important for the production of cumulative deuterium in the interactions of oxygen with protons at 3.25GeV/c per nucleon.

the contribution to the total cross section for production of the cumulative deuterons from the processes of slow-pion absorption on alpha-particle clusters amounts to approximately 20% of the total cross section.
the processes of the decay of the clusters of alpha particles in nuclei upon slowpion absorption by these nuclei are the main source of cumulative-deuterons production in 16OP interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the production of cumulative deuterium nuclei in 16Op reactions can be described by a mechanism that is similar to that of the production of other cumulative nuclei.

cumulative deuterons are produced in 16Op reactions at a momentum of p = 3.25 (A/2) GeV/c per proton and that the contribution to their production from the slow-pion absorption process by the alpha-particle cluster in the nucleus is not small.

the production of cumulative nuclei in the interaction of nuclei with a momentum of 1.6 GeV/c per proton with a proton is a process that occurs at a low energy and can be used to investigate the properties of the nuclear medium.
